package_info.package_manager: N/A (custom exploit tool, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: Affects all supported Windows versions (Windows 10/11, fully patched as of 2024-10)
package_info.why_malicious: The tool enables attackers to downgrade critical Windows system components (DLLs, drivers, kernel) to older, vulnerable versions, bypassing security controls and reintroducing patched vulnerabilities. This allows unsigned kernel drivers to be loaded, disables security features, and enables further malicious activity while evading detection.

execution_context.file_location: ci.dll (Windows Code Integrity module), other system DLLs/drivers

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Downdate tool logic: Overwrite patched system DLL (e.g., ci.dll) with an older, vulnerable version, bypassing Windows file protection and update mechanisms.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the tool replaces a patched system DLL (such as ci.dll) with an older, vulnerable version, reintroducing previously patched vulnerabilities and bypassing digital signature enforcement.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Overwriting protected system files with older, vulnerable versions is a classic privilege escalation and persistence technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal system operation expects system DLLs to be immutable and only updated via trusted Windows Update mechanisms. Downgrading to vulnerable versions is never legitimate.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate system recovery or rollback tools may restore previous versions, but only with explicit user/admin consent and logging.
key_indicators: Direct modification of system DLLs (e.g., ci.dll) outside of Windows Update
Bypassing file immutability and digital signature enforcement

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Exploit logic: Trigger page faults to force Windows to reload and allow modification of files marked as immutable, exploiting 'False File Immutability' (ItsNotASecurityBoundary).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the exploit triggers page faults to bypass file immutability, allowing modification of protected files in memory and on disk, enabling further exploitation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bypassing file immutability to modify protected system files is a clear sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Protected system files should not be modifiable after being locked by the OS. Exploiting page fault handling to alter them is highly abnormal.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use; this is a direct exploitation of a security boundary.
key_indicators: Triggering page faults to modify protected files
Modifying files with write access explicitly denied
Targeting files patched for known vulnerabilities

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Load unsigned kernel driver: Use the downgraded, vulnerable ci.dll to load an unsigned or malicious kernel driver.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker loads an unsigned or malicious kernel driver using the downgraded ci.dll, bypassing digital signature enforcement and enabling arbitrary code execution in kernel mode.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading unsigned drivers on a fully patched system is a major red flag, as it bypasses core Windows security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Windows should only allow signed drivers to be loaded, especially on Secure Boot-enabled systems.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate driver development/testing may require test signing, but never on production systems without explicit configuration.
key_indicators: Loading unsigned drivers on a system with Secure Boot and DSE enabled
Driver loads following suspicious DLL downgrades
Kernel-level code execution without proper signatures

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains administrative or SYSTEM-level access to the target Windows system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to execute custom tools and modify system files

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the Downdate tool to overwrite patched system DLLs (e.g., ci.dll) with older, vulnerable versions.
attack_chain.leads_to: System is now running with known-vulnerable components

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits 'False File Immutability' by triggering page faults to modify protected files, bypassing write restrictions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Further modification of system files and persistence

attack_chain.action: Attacker loads unsigned or malicious kernel drivers using the downgraded ci.dll, bypassing digital signature enforcement.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full kernel-level code execution, disabling security features, deploying rootkits, etc.

attack_chain.action: Attacker disables security features, deploys and disguises malicious code and processes, and maintains persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: complete system compromise and evasion of detection

behavioral_signatures: Unexplained downgrades of system DLLs or drivers to older, vulnerable versions
Modification of protected system files outside of Windows Update
Loading of unsigned kernel drivers on Secure Boot-enabled systems
Page fault activity correlated with file modifications on protected files
file_indicators: ci.dll or other system DLLs replaced with older versions
Timestamps or hashes of system files not matching expected values
Presence of custom tools/scripts capable of DLL/driver replacement
network_indicators: Outbound connections for downloading old/vulnerable DLLs or drivers
Potential C2 traffic if malicious drivers establish persistence
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for changes to system DLLs and drivers, especially downgrades to known-vulnerable versions. Alert on any modification of protected files outside of Windows Update. Detect attempts to load unsigned drivers on systems with Secure Boot or DSE enabled. Correlate page fault activity with file modifications on protected files. Use file integrity monitoring and maintain a baseline of expected system file versions and hashes.
